newsitem.title: USA: Patent auction seen impacting Intel - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Patent auction seen impacting Intel - WSJ.

text.p: Big semiconductor companies are preparing to bid for patents held by a defunct Silicon Valley company that could make it easier to compete with or license patents from Intel Corp, the Wall Street Journal reported.
The patents could also affect Intel's pending litigation with Digital Equipment Corp, the paper added.
The failed company -- Exponential Technology Inc -- is preparing to auction off its portfolio of 45 issued and pending microprocessor-related patents next week.
In addition to Intel and Digital, some expected bidders include Advanced Micro Devices Inc and Cyrix Corp , the paper said.

The Exponential patents are believed to include inventions that could help develop next-generation microprocessor chips that match features of forthcoming Intel products, the paper said, citing industry executives and analysts.

The patents could enable competitors to clone Merced, a long-awaited chip which Intel is designing with Hewlett-Packard Co, and reduce the risks of an Intel suit for patent infringement, the paper said.
